boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase outings for exploring Harvard’s museums, galleries, landscapes, architecture, history, and public art together.

cards.title: Roam Three Art Collections Under One Roof
cards.subtitle: A free gallery hang on Quincy Street
cards.notes: Meet beneath the Calderwood Courtyard roof, choose a gallery theme together, and compare favorite works before regrouping downstairs.
cards.short_summary: Browse more than 50 galleries spanning the Fogg, Busch-Reisinger, and Arthur M. Sackler museums without buying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard states that the Harvard Art Museums are free and open to all visitors Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Open to all visitors Tuesday through Sunday; consult the museum’s current visitor information before arriving.

cards.entity_name: Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East
cards.title: Explore the Ancient Near East Together
cards.subtitle: A free archaeology outing on Divinity Avenue
cards.notes: Start at the entrance, split up to inspect different artifacts, then reunite and share one object or inscription that caught your attention.
cards.short_summary: Turn a free museum visit into a group conversation about artifacts and cultures from the ancient Near East.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Museums of Science & Culture lists general admission to the Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East as free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Harvard Museums of Science & Culture
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; the official visit page lists Sunday–Friday opening and scheduled closure information.

cards.title: Compare Centuries of Scientific Tools
cards.subtitle: A free Science Center gallery challenge
cards.notes: Browse the instrument cases with friends and each select one device to explain, sketch, or use as the starting point for a trivia question.
cards.short_summary: Make a social scavenger hunt from Harvard’s historic clocks, calculators, laboratory tools, and other scientific instruments.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Museums of Science & Culture lists general admission to the Collection of Historical Scientific Instruments as free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Harvard Museums of Science & Culture
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; the official visit page lists Sunday–Friday hours and notes scheduled gallery closures.

cards.title: Bring a Friend to the Natural History Galleries
cards.subtitle: Free entry with a current Harvard ID, plus one guest
cards.notes: Bring your Harvard ID, invite one guest, and trade turns choosing the next gallery—from glass flowers and minerals to fossils and wildlife.
cards.short_summary: Use the Harvard ID benefit for a two-person natural-history outing with no admission purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: The official HMSC visit page states that current Harvard ID holders receive free admission to the Harvard Museum of Natural History plus one guest.
cards.source_title: Visit | Harvard Museums of Science & Culture
cards.access_notes: A current Harvard ID is required for the free holder-plus-one-guest benefit; general public admission otherwise requires payment.

cards.title: Trade Perspectives in the Peabody Galleries
cards.subtitle: Free entry with a current Harvard ID, plus one guest
cards.notes: Bring your Harvard ID and a guest, pick separate galleries to explore, then meet back up to exchange observations about two objects.
cards.short_summary: Share an archaeology and ethnology visit through Harvard’s free ID-holder admission benefit.
cards.evidence_claim: The official HMSC visit page states that current Harvard ID holders receive free admission to the Peabody Museum plus one guest.
cards.source_title: Visit | Harvard Museums of Science & Culture
cards.access_notes: A current Harvard ID is required for the free holder-plus-one-guest benefit; general public admission otherwise requires payment.

cards.title: Take a No-Cost Arboretum Walk
cards.subtitle: A free landscape outing among living collections
cards.notes: Choose an official self-guided route, meet at an agreed gate, and walk the collections together while recording seasonal plant discoveries.
cards.short_summary: Spend a morning or afternoon walking Harvard’s 281-acre living collection without paying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arnold Arboretum states that its landscape is open daily, free for everyone to explore, and always free of admission.
cards.access_notes: The landscape is open daily from sunrise to sunset and admission is always free; Visitor Center hours are more limited.

cards.entity_name: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Pair Contemporary Art with Le Corbusier Architecture
cards.subtitle: A free exhibition hang on Quincy Street
cards.notes: Walk the ramp together, examine the current installations, and pause outside to compare how the building shapes your experience of the art.
cards.short_summary: Combine changing contemporary-art exhibitions with a close look at Le Corbusier’s only North American building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carpenter Center identifies itself as free and open to the public and states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during posted gallery hours; check the official site for exhibition transitions and closure days.

cards.entity_name: Alain Locke Gallery of African & African American Art
cards.title: Discuss Art at the Alain Locke Gallery
cards.subtitle: An always-free Hutchins Center exhibition outing
cards.notes: Visit with a classmate, read the curatorial text before separating, and regroup to discuss how two selected works approach history or culture.
cards.short_summary: Use a free gallery visit to encounter exhibitions centered on African, African American, and Afro-Latin American art.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official Harvard website states that the Alain Locke Gallery is always free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Alain Locke Gallery of African & African American Art
cards.access_notes: Always free and open to the public; confirm current exhibition dates and gallery hours on the official site before visiting.

cards.title: Join Harvard’s Free Historical Tour
cards.subtitle: A student-led walk through Harvard Yard
cards.notes: Reserve spaces for your group, arrive early at the designated meeting point, and bring one campus-history question for the student guide.
cards.short_summary: Hear university history and a student guide’s perspective while walking through Harvard Yard at no charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard describes its Official Historical Tour as a free, student-led public walking tour through Harvard Yard.
cards.access_notes: The in-person tour requires registration; consult the official tour page for current availability, meeting instructions, and campus access rules.

cards.entity_name: Harvard Public Art & Culture Tour: Cambridge
cards.title: Follow the Cambridge Public-Art Trail
cards.subtitle: A free self-guided tour in Harvard’s mobile app
cards.notes: Download the free tour or open its desktop version, choose a starting stop together, and take turns narrating the art and architecture entries.
cards.short_summary: Explore outdoor art, notable architecture, and Harvard cultural institutions on a self-paced group walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard says its free mobile app includes the self-guided Harvard Public Art & Culture Tour: Cambridge; a desktop experience is also available.
cards.access_notes: The self-guided tour is available through Harvard’s free mobile app and desktop experience; observe posted building and campus access restrictions.
